rows.grounds: subject of third clause, also understood as fruitful

items.question: Which aspects of the devoted practitioner attain true fruitfulness?
premises: Initiation becomes fruitful for the devoted practitioner.
Ritual action becomes fruitful for the devoted practitioner.
The practitioner's body becomes fruitful through devotion.
items.inference: Therefore initiation, ritual action, and the body all attain fruitfulness for such a devotee.
uncertainties: The predicate saphalā is expressed twice but applies implicitly to tanuḥ as well.
items.plain_english: Indeed, O Goddess, initiation is fruitful, ritual action is fruitful, and the body is fruitful.
